problem_statement:
Creating an issue from a template doesn't apply template labels to newly created issue
### Describe the bug

When creating an issue using `gh issue create` and selecting a template, the labels associated with that template are not assigned to the issue upon creation.

```
$ gh version
gh version 0.7.0 (2020-04-22)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.7.0
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `gh issue create` (against a repo that has issue templates with labels associated with each)
2. Fill in info
3. Create issue without previewing in browser
4. Observe that issue was not assigned labels associated with template that was chosen

### Expected vs actual behavior

If a template was chosen that has labels, those labels should be assigned to the issue when created via `gh issue create`

### Logs

```console
$ gh issue create

Creating issue in intel/dffml

? Choose a template Missing Documentation
? Title docs: cli: edit command
? Body <Received>
? What's next? Submit
https://github.com/intel/dffml/issues/616
```

"json: cannot unmarshal string" error message for unsuccessful "gh api" request
### Describe the bug

From within a GitHub Actions workflow, I want to delete review requests using `gh api`, but I get both an HTTP 422 response and an error message.

I'm using the `gh` version provided in the Ubuntu 18.04 GitHub-hosted runners, version 0.11.0 currently.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

I use

```sh
gh api "repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/$prid/requested_reviewers" \
    --method DELETE --input - --silent --include < reviewers.json
```

where `$prid` is the pull request ID and `reviewers.json` looks something like

```json
{
  "reviewers": [
    "user1",
    "user2"
  ]
}
```

The returned headers show that this fails with

```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
```

and I get an error

```
json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field .Errors of type struct { Message string }
```

By now, I understand that the reason for the 422 is a permission issue; using curl for the same request results in the more descriptive error

```json
{
  "message": "Validation Failed",
  "errors": [
    "Could not resolve to a node with the global id of '<redacted>'."
  ],
  "documentation_url": "https://developer.github.com/v3/pulls/review_requests/#delete-a-review-request"
}
```

and using a personal access token instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN` works. (I wonder why that's required, though, and asked about it [here](https://github.community/t/cannot-remove-review-request-from-within-workflow/125473?u=bewuethr).)

### Expected vs actual behavior

I'd probably expect the client to handle the error case more gracefully than bubbling up the json unmarshalling error, and showing the actual error message would be helpful, too.

### Logs

The complete output from `--include` and the response itself:

```

Access-Control-Expose-Headers: ETag, Link, Location, Retry-After, X-GitHub-OTP, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, X-OAuth-Scopes, X-Accepted-OAuth-Scopes, X-Poll-Interval, X-GitHub-Media-Type, Deprecation, Sunset
```

repo create: local directory for new repo not created when non-interactive and --confirm
### Describe the bug

Not sure if it is a bug or undocumented feature: It looks like when capturing the output of `gh repo create`, local folder is not created (while it is when running without output capture).

```
gh --version
gh version 1.3.1 (2020-12-03)
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Be outside of an existing local `git` directory.
2. Run `echo $(gh repo create org/repo --private --confirm)`
3. The repository is created on github.com, but no local folder is initialized/created.

Changing step 2 to `gh repo create org/repo --private --confirm` will initialize folder locally.

### Expected behavior

Consistent behavior (with/without encapsulating the command), or documentation of the "feature" on https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_create.

rls: Do not use `cmp` package in non-test code
Currently, `rls/internal/keys/builder.go` uses `cmp.Equal`.

The `cmp` package documentation says the following:
It is intended to only be used in tests, as performance is not a goal and it may panic if it cannot compare the values. Its propensity towards panicking means that its unsuitable for production environments where a spurious panic may be fatal.

2. Go to a repository directory that uses that server as a remote
3. Run `gh run list` (This should work)
4. Pick one of the run numbers and run `gh run view <number>`

### Expected vs actual behavior

The client should show the details of the run, but instead fails with HTTP 404

problem_statement:
`gh pr list --state=closed` excludes `merged` — differs from `is:closed` behavior on web UI?
### Describe the UX question

Not a bug but a UX question / inconsistency: is it confusing that official `gh` CLI models "merged" PRs as disjoint set from "closed", whereas the web site mostly treats merging as "kind of closing"?

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `gh pr list --state=closed` shows only PRs that were closed without merging (red).
2. `gh pr list --state=merged` shows only PRs that were merged (purple)

On the other hand when searching on github.com:

1. Search `is:pr state:closed` returns PRs both "closed by merging" (purple) and closed without merging (red).
2. `state:merged` syntax not supported :slightly_frowning_face: 

To compare 2 other CLI tools: 
- `hub pr list --state=closed` is superset (red and purple) of `hub pr list --state=merged` (purple only).
- `ghi --no-pager list --pulls --state=closed` returns both closed and merged, with no indication which is which.  `--state=merged` not supported.  (Which is to be expected from a tool specializing in issues, and only supporting PRs because github kinda pretends PRs are a kind of issues.)

### Discussion

If you look at color coding, PRs consistenly have 3 states: green open / red closed / purple merged.  No problems there.

Arguably, this tool works fine, it's the github.com search syntax that confuses things.  And that probably happened because it searches both PRs and issues (unless you filter by `is:pr`), and issues have only binary open/closed state.
(Arguably that's the root problem: there is no concept of issues being "closed as fixed" vs "closed as wontfix".  Somewhat understandable as there are grey areas of "can't reproduce", "too old", "issue bankrupcy", "mitigated", "hopefully fixed", "fixed on some platforms" etc... :grinning: so it was just left to free-form text and labels.)

Part of the problem is **terminology**: the lack of distinct words for "closed without merging" vs "either closed or merged" makes even discussing this painful.
If you want to untangle this, inventing a new term for one of them would be good...

Improvements to `label list`
Based on [comments](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/5452#discussion_r854456986), I think there's a few improvements we should make to `label list`:

* [x] Do not limit results by default. There seems to be no customer value unless they explicitly want to limit results.

  To clarify, it is used as the page size and does support paging, but lines 67-69 of this block of code should be removed:

  https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/c99c47f34db5d1ff742ae2bb89a64d7b6fb2aa06/pkg/cmd/label/list/http.go#L65-L70

* [x] One reason they might want to limit results is to filter the list, much like you can filter issues or PRs. Like [heaths/gh-label](https://github.com/heaths/gh-label) we could either tag an optional argument for the filter term, or a `--search` parameter like `issue list` has for consistency. The former would only be breaking if someone actually expected an error with an additional arg, but that seems like an impractical test. The latter would be consistent with `issue list` and `pr list`, however.
* [x] Sort results by default. A large list of unsorted labels is difficult to read and find what you want. The order returned is also not documented and should not be relied on.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/pkg/cmd/label/delete.go
@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+package label
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/AlecAivazis/survey/v2"
+	"github.com/cli/cli/v2/api"
+	"github.com/cli/cli/v2/internal/ghrepo"
+	"github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/cmdutil"
+	"github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/iostreams"
+	"github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/prompt"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+type deleteOptions struct {
+	BaseRepo   func() (ghrepo.Interface, error)
+	HttpClient func() (*http.Client, error)
+	IO         *iostreams.IOStreams
+
+	Name      string
+	Confirmed bool
+}
+
+func newCmdDelete(f *cmdutil.Factory, runF func(*deleteOptions) error) *cobra.Command {
+	opts := deleteOptions{
+		HttpClient: f.HttpClient,
+		IO:         f.IOStreams,
+	}
+
+	cmd := &cobra.Command{
+		Use:   "delete <name>",
+		Short: "Delete a label from a repository",
+		Args:  cmdutil.ExactArgs(1, "cannot delete label: name argument required"),
+		RunE: func(c *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+			// support `-R, --repo` override
+			opts.BaseRepo = f.BaseRepo
+			opts.Name = args[0]
+
+			if !opts.IO.CanPrompt() && !opts.Confirmed {
+				return cmdutil.FlagErrorf("--confirm required when not running interactively")
+			}
+
+			if runF != nil {
+				return runF(&opts)
+			}
+			return deleteRun(&opts)
+		},
+	}
+
+	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&opts.Confirmed, "confirm", false, "Confirm deletion without prompting")
+
+	return cmd
+}
+
+func deleteRun(opts *deleteOptions) error {
+	httpClient, err := opts.HttpClient()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	baseRepo, err := opts.BaseRepo()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	if !opts.Confirmed {
+		var valid string
+		err := prompt.SurveyAskOne(
+			&survey.Input{Message: fmt.Sprintf("Type %s to confirm deletion:", opts.Name)},
+			&valid,
+			survey.WithValidator(
+				func(val interface{}) error {
+					if str := val.(string); !strings.EqualFold(str, opts.Name) {
+						return fmt.Errorf("You entered %s", str)
+					}
+					return nil
+				}))
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("could not prompt: %w", err)
+		}
+	}
+
+	opts.IO.StartProgressIndicator()
+	err = deleteLabel(httpClient, baseRepo, opts.Name)
+	opts.IO.StopProgressIndicator()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	if opts.IO.IsStdoutTTY() {
+		cs := opts.IO.ColorScheme()
+		successMsg := fmt.Sprintf("%s Label %q deleted from %s\n", cs.SuccessIcon(), opts.Name, ghrepo.FullName(baseRepo))
+		fmt.Fprint(opts.IO.Out, successMsg)
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+func deleteLabel(client *http.Client, repo ghrepo.Interface, name string) error {
+	apiClient := api.NewClientFromHTTP(client)
+	path := fmt.Sprintf("repos/%s/%s/labels/%s", repo.RepoOwner(), repo.RepoName(), name)
+
+	return apiClient.REST(repo.RepoHost(), "DELETE", path, nil, nil)
+}

problem_statement:
Include all branches when creating repository from template
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

When creating a repository from a template it is possible to specify whether or not all branches in the template repository should be included in the new repository. However (as far as I can tell), it does not appear possible to specify this option from the CLI. It would be good if this could be added as an additional option.

### Proposed solution

Add a new boolean flag to the [create command](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmd/repo/create/create.go). The flag should decide if all branches should be included when creating from a template. Can only be used when creating from a template.

[Map the flag to the corresponding input](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2df3dd4f7dd98e7969e6d9b760f0725aac8a2158/pkg/cmd/repo/create/http.go#L106) for the mutation. Input name is `includeAllBranches` and is documented [here](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/input-objects#clonetemplaterepositoryinput).

How will it benefit CLI and its users?

It will allow CLI users the same options as when creating a repository from template using the github.com website.

### Additional context

Add any other context like screenshots or mockups are helpful, if applicable.

Sometimes gRPC client cannot send RPCs when the DNS server is temporarily unavailable
The dns resolver sets an empty address list to the balancer when it got an error from DNS server.
Then gRPC client cannot send RPCs for a while because the picker cannot get an address to use for requests until addresses were set to the balancer.

### What version of gRPC are you using?

1.25.1 or later

### What version of Go are you using (`go version`)?

1.13.4

### What operating system (Linux, Windows, …) and version?

Linux

### What did you do?

I made sure that whether the gRPC client can send an RPC to the server when the DNS server is temporarily unavailable.

1. I deployed `5` pods as echo-server and 1 pod as greet-client to kubernetes cluster.
    - I created echo-server and greet-client based on [examples/helloworld](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/tree/master/examples/helloworld).
    - greet-client is working with client-side round-robin load balancer and sends an RPC to echo-server every 300ms.
1. I deleted several pods of kube-dns to reproduce situations when DNS server is temporarily unavailable.
1. I deleted 1 pod of echo-server.

### What did you expect to see?

I expect greet-client to send an RPC to one of the remaining `4` pods of echo-server.

### What did you see instead?

I got `rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = latest balancer error: resolver returned no addresses` error.
And the error continues until the next DNS lookup is succeeded (maybe more than 30s).

Below is client log output.
```
INFO: 2019/12/13 06:59:05 roundrobinPicker: newPicker called with info: {map[0xc000102140:{{10.42.0.27:5000  <nil> 0 <nil>}} 0xc000102160:{{10.42.3.32:5000  <nil> 0 <nil>}} 0xc000102190:{{10.42.1.23:5000  <nil> 0 <nil>}} 0xc0001021d0:{{10.42.2.28:5000  <nil> 0 <nil>}}]}
WARNING: 2019/12/13 06:59:05 grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect to {10.42.4.19:5000  <nil> 0 <nil>}. Err :connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 10.42.4.19:5000: connect: connection refused". Reconnecting...
WARNING: 2019/12/13 06:59:10 grpc: failed dns A record lookup due to lookup echo-server-hs.echo-server.svc.cluster.local: Try again.
INFO: 2019/12/13 06:59:10 ccResolverWrapper: sending update to cc: {[] <nil> <nil>}
INFO: 2019/12/13 06:59:10 roundrobinPicker: newPicker called with info: {map[]}
INFO: 2019/12/13 06:59:10 roundrobinPicker: newPicker called with info: {map[]}
INFO: 2019/12/13 06:59:10 roundrobinPicker: newPicker called with info: {map[]}
WARNING: 2019/12/13 06:59:10 grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect to {10.42.4.19:5000  <nil> 0 <nil>}. Err :connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 10.42.4.19:5000: operation was canceled". Reconnecting...

ERROR: 2019/12/13 06:59:11 rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = latest balancer error: resolver returned no addresses

```

For now, it seems the dns resolver [ignores an error returned from the DNS server](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/085c980048876e2735d4aba8f0d5bca4d7acaaa5/internal/resolver/dns/dns_resolver.go#L289:L292).
It should be handled, and the dns resolver should be not set an empty address list to balancer when it got an error from the DNS server.

grpclb: fallback gracefully if no balancer addresses are provided
grpclb can be selected by `loadBalancingConfig` (in addition to the traditional "are there balancer addresses in the resolved address list" case), and if no balancer addresses are present when selected this way, the current grpclb implementation will be unhappy.  This needs to be handled more gracefully in case the scenario occurs, to prevent the client from being wedged.

Re-resolution loop when service config is not supported
### What version of gRPC are you using?

v1.25.0 or later

### What version of Go are you using (`go version`)?

`go version go1.13.4 darwin/amd64`

### What operating system (Linux, Windows, …) and version?

Mac, Linux

### What did you do?
If possible, provide a recipe for reproducing the error.

### What did you expect to see?

For DNS resolver, the default frequency of DNS resolution is 30 minutes, so DNS resolution happens every 30 minutes.

### What did you see instead?

For DNS resolver, the minimum duration for re-resolution is set to 30 seconds by `minDNSResRate`. When Service Config is invalid, DNS resolution happens every 30 seconds. This happens even if service config feature is not used, which means txt lookup returns error.

This is because of [polling](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.25.x/resolver_conn_wrapper.go#L221-L231) that is introduced from v1.25.0 for error handling. The `NewServiceConfig` is called from resolver when service config is updated. 
In DNS resolver, [watcher](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/v1.25.x/internal/resolver/dns/dns_resolver.go#L267) calls NewServiceConfig. The polling calls `ResolveNow` to do immediate re-resolution, so the request of dns resolution is queued in dns resolver. The request also makes a call of `NewServiceConfig`, so it becomes infinite loop.

If a resolver calls NewServiceConfig as a result of ResolveNow, the resolver possibly becomes loops. I'm not sure which part is bad, but NewServiceConfig should not be called when service config is disabled and it is better to have backoff for re-resolution.
